text:
Maria (eng-runtime): heads-up: after yesterday's kernel-picker tweak I’m seeing p99 latency regressions on small-chat workloads. diffs look like more microbatch fragmentation and higher queue churn. :frowning:
Jin: can you paste a quick flame or profiler snap? also kv-hit rates around the same?
Maria (eng-runtime): paste from the 11:03 canary below — noticed kernel switch to `fast-attn-v2` more often, but batches smaller.
```
perf.snapshot: p50=22ms p95=127ms p99=298ms
batch_size: mean=6 median=4 p95=18
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.62
kernel_selected: fast-attn-v2 (60%), fallback: generic-attn (40%)
```
Kevin: interesting — if kernel hinting nudges to fast-attn earlier it can reduce batching affinity. smaller batches -> higher per-token overhead. might need a tiny admission reservation to avoid micro-fragmentation.
Tara: +1. propose soft-burst window: reserve N tokens for the head of queue for X ms to allow coalescing. reduces microbatches without blocking long-tail latency.
Leo: admit-bot just posted alerts for queue depth spikes during the roll: `queue_depth>200` and `microbatch_evictions=34` between 10:58-11:05. link: https://deploys/reports/roll/28625
admit-bot: alert: queue_spike detected on canary pool A | peak_q=217 | evictions=34 | avg_wait=48ms
Jin: for the experiment, I suggest paramizing: `soft_burst_window_ms=10`, `reserve_token_budget=64`, `max_soft_reject_rate=0.08`. run against canary and compare p99 and unit-cost.
Kevin: put a small config snippet we can push to canary (TBD):
```
admission:
  mode: soft_burst
  soft_burst_window_ms: 10
  reserve_token_budget: 64
  soft_429_threshold: 0.08
  kernel_pref_hint_ttl_ms: 150
```
Tara: question on soft_429: do we return a synthetic soft-429 payload or allow background defer-to-fallback? we should fallback to cheaper model variant before emitting 429s for PLG paths. @Maria thoughts?
Maria (eng-runtime): fallback before soft-429. for interactive chat prefer degrade gracefully. hard 429s only when queue > 800 or eviction rate > 0.2.
Jin: checklist: 1) run canary with snippet, 2) collect `batch_size_distribution`, `kv_hit_by_batch`, `kernel_switch_rate`, `p99_latency` for 30m windows, 3) compare unit token cost delta. 4) add a microprobe that increases kernel hint TTL if kv_hit_rate>0.7 (to keep affinity).
Leo: I'll attach a tiny log snippet of a problematic request flow:
```
[11:02:15] req=abcd kernel=fast-attn-v2 batch=2 queued=27 wait=72ms -> evicted
[11:02:16] req=efgh kernel=generic-attn batch=9 queued=5 wait=12ms -> served
```
Maria (eng-runtime): sounds good. I'll schedule the canary experiment in the A/B runner for 11:45 and tag you all. quick win if p99 drops without cost increase. :thumbsup:
Kevin: if this stabilizes, follow-up is to add kernel-aware token budgeting in the admission controller (kernel-specific reserve sizes).
Tara: SGTM. thanks everyone.
